findings.title: Commit meter is not guaranteed to measure system commit
findings.finding: Cmt derives used/limit from MEMORYSTATUSEX ullTotalPageFile and ullAvailPageFile. Those fields may reflect current-process limits and commit availability rather than whole-system CommitTotal/CommitLimit. Merely renaming inherited PageMemory to commit did not prove the intended host metric.
findings.closure: Use GetPerformanceInfo/PERFORMANCE_INFORMATION CommitTotal and CommitLimit with PageSize, explicit state and overflow checks, or label and expose the exact process-constrained scope. Test under a job/process memory limit and compare an independent system-commit observer.

findings.title: Process CPU deltas use a different observation window from system denominator
findings.finding: GetSystemTimes before is read before the whole first process pass; after is read before the second pass. Each process CPU interval is shifted by per-process read cost, but CPU% divides by the common system delta without own elapsed time. Variable pass costs can bias percentages, especially short intervals/large process sets. A separate documented GetSystemTimes processor-group limitation remains.
findings.closure: Define and implement per-process monotonic sample bounds/CPU capacity or a consistently sampled native provider. Test delayed individual reads and changing process counts with independent expected values. Either handle processor groups or report unavailable/explicit scoped metric on unsupported topology.

findings.title: Bulk mutation results lose per-target outcomes
findings.finding: Priority loops repeatedly overwrite one status message; termination retains only success/failure counts after overwriting detail. A later success can hide an earlier denied/failed target. Identity is revalidated, but required individual result reporting is incomplete.
findings.closure: Collect bounded per-target structured outcomes, display a summary with inspectable failures, and use the same result type for future CLI actions. Test mixed success/denied/exited/reused identities against owned fixtures.

findings.classification: source-confirmed feature gap and documented risk
findings.title: Slow/stalled samples remain displayed without freshness state
findings.finding: Synchronous account-name lookup is inside the single collector. Published values have no sample-age/stale display; LastSampleElapsed changes only after completion. Main loop can continue rendering old values as ordinary measurements.
findings.closure: Add publication timestamps, stale/missed/degraded status and bounded provider policy. Fault-inject a blocked lookup. Cache or isolate expensive lookup only with explicit ownership; a timeout is not cancellation.

findings.priority: P1 to close user-requested bar contract; not a crash finding
findings.title: Function bar is implemented but fully contextual/live status is incomplete
findings.finding: Bar is default visible, hideable and clickable, with static F1-F10 labels in every panel. Persistent active-filter/sort/provider/freshness status is not implemented; adjacent row is only allocated for prompt/message/Emacs prefix.
findings.closure: Implement a shared context-action/hint table plus concise active-view/filter/sort/dirty/freshness status, keeping hidden-bar recovery and narrow geometry correct.

findings.priority: P1 qualify supported encoding before 0.4.0; richer shaping may be later
findings.title: UTF-16 code-unit length is used as display-cell width
findings.finding: Clipping, RenderColumn, tab hit widths and editor cursor mostly count UTF-16 units, with only surrogate-pair boundary protection. CJK wide characters, combining sequences and host-specific width can misalign display and hitboxes.
findings.closure: Implement explicit cell-width policy with conservative substitution where necessary; test ASCII, wide/combining/surrogate inputs and every supported host. Do not claim all-Unicode layout from UTF-8 configuration parsing.

findings.classification: source-confirmed storage limitation; race not reproduced
findings.priority: P1 before claiming safe installed settings
findings.title: Settings replacement does not preserve custom ACLs and is not atomic CAS
findings.finding: Two byte-equality checks detect many stale edits but a writer can change an existing target between final check and MoveFileEx replacement. A newly created temporary file is renamed over target without metadata/ACL transfer.
findings.closure: Specify concurrent-writer contract; choose a qualified replacement/metadata strategy preserving intended ACLs and attributes. Test two instances/editor race, denied paths, disk-full and interrupted replacement.

findings.priority: P1 policy before first stable CLI promise
findings.title: Literal htop CLI parity conflicts with Wtop aliases
findings.finding: Wtop -d selects dump/snapshot; stable htop 3.5.3 -d expects decisecond delay. Wtop inherited -n means names; development htop 3.6.0-dev uses -n for max iterations, but stable 3.5.3 does not. Most htop long aliases and several distinct behaviors are not implemented.
findings.closure: Freeze an explicit compatibility table. Preserve NTop aliases deliberately; decide -d before first stable release. Prefer nonambiguous long options and document deviations instead of blanket parity.

findings.priority: P2 measurement gate for 0.4.0; optimize when evidence warrants
findings.title: Flat-view sorting still builds process tree and frames redraw in full
findings.finding: FindParentChildProcesses scans process pairs and ancestry and runs after flat sorting too. DrawFrame clears every row and rewrites it; per-cell colors/cursor/output use multiple API calls. These are plausible scaling/remote-output hotspots, not a measured regression.
findings.closure: Benchmark process-count/terminal-size/interval matrix, collect CPU/handles/memory/output bytes and responsiveness. Only then remove unused tree work, index identities/parents or coalesce/dirty-render output with behavioral checks.

findings.classification: documented lifecycle risk and missing qualification
findings.title: Emergency self-exit does not qualify orderly shutdown on blocked native calls
findings.finding: Initial snapshot runs on main thread. TUI main thread also holds SyncLock around input/render and explicit save. Normal cleanup joins for 3000 ms; CtrlHandler waits 3500 ms and may TerminateProcess self, bypassing restoration if main has not reached cleanup. No native fault-injection or handle-soak evidence closes this broad contract.
findings.closure: Exercise provider/output/settings stalls, Ctrl+C/close/error/resize, repeated launches and normal/emergency exit. Define and expose emergency behavior; qualify isolation only if used. No claim of zero leaks/crashes from compile or normal-path smoke.

findings.priority: P2 UX; can remain documented 0.4.0 limit if scope agrees
findings.title: Tabs support configuration creation but no TUI create/rename/delete
findings.finding: Up to eight named views and per-view filter/sort/direction/tree/columns exist. F2 can hide/reorder existing tabs; create, rename and delete require file editing. Column widths are responsive constants, not user-defined. Keymaps are presets, not arbitrary declarative rebinding.
findings.closure: Either retain and clearly document bounded 0.4.0 scope or add small TUI CRUD/edit operations with round-trip validation. Do not repeat the claim as missing all customization.

findings.title: Formal acceptance and evidence registers remain unpromoted
findings.finding: specctl reports 51 not_run, 1 active/14 planned, 0 evidence records, 15 unqualified targets and 1 policy-blocked. Real native CI exists separately. Whole-product gates must not be marked passed by narrow CI, but stale work status obscures completed implementation.
findings.closure: Reconcile source-bound narrow observations, split broad acceptance into reviewable scoped cases where necessary, and advance only satisfied work. Build an exact 0.4.0 feature/profile closure.

findings.priority: P1 if advertised in 0.4.0; otherwise explicitly later scope
findings.title: No managed packaging/install channels or portable ownership mode
findings.finding: Current backend has adjacent/legacy/user config discovery and config export, not installed portable/per-user/machine ownership, migration, updater/rollback/uninstall, setup EXE/MSI or WinGet manifests. Merely distributing one EXE does not complete installation modes.
findings.closure: Package exact qualified payload with honest target metadata, checksums/license/source correspondence and reversible owned PATH/registration. Preserve settings outside payload ownership. Only publish channels actually built/installed/uninstalled/tested.

findings.title: Full low-level CLI, htop feature superset and historical backends are unimplemented
findings.finding: Current application supports only Windows NT x86/x64/ARM64 compile profiles, simple snapshots and build-capabilities metadata. Query/inspect/continuous bounded logging, runtime provider negotiation, full commands/threads/details/affinity/per-core telemetry and DOS/Win16/Win9x/CE/OS2 providers do not exist. GUI is explicitly deferred.
findings.closure: Implement capability-based vertical slices and qualify exact target images. Preserve all requested families as goals with explicit feasibility/support decisions; blocked/unavailable is not fabricated completion.
